summary: Marion County fire tower near Yellville; a 1954 survey describes a wooden tower about 120 ft high, and 1943-47 newspaper notices name its staff. Current status unknown.

facts.design: four-legged wooden structure with an observation cabin
facts.status_note: The newest dated account found is the 1954 survey description; the newest staffing notice is from February 1947. No current source confirms that the tower stands.

events.note: Birth notice from The Mountaineer Echo, as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, reports a daughter born at the Freck fire tower.
Birth notice from The Mountaineer Echo places Lester E. Delano at the fire tower south of Yellville.
Notice says Harry Elmer Smith assumed the duties at the fire tower south of Yellville, replacing Lester Delano, who had been there for several months.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: four-legged wood structure about 120 feet high, supporting an observation cabin.

sources.title: Freck - FOREST LOOKOUTS (quotes The Mountaineer Echo, 1943 to 1947; reproduces NGS station description PID GF0707)

notes_for_editor: Single web source. The 1943-1947 newspaper items are quoted second-hand from The Mountaineer Echo on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspaper itself was not checked. The 1954 Coast and Geodetic Survey description is the only physical description and matches the brief height (36.6 m = about 120 ft). Nothing found on build date, fire record, fate or current condition; the brief's unknown status is kept. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the story's latest-dated-item line was wrong, because the 1954 survey description is later than the February 1947 notice. The story now names the 1954 description as the latest dated account and the 1947 notice as the latest staffing report. The April 28, 1943, October 3, 1946 and February 13, 1947 dates were checked against the page. Searches: two web searches (results were cemetery and town pages, nothing on the tower beyond the Forest Lookouts page); the Anyplace America topo page returned 403. The ARGenWeb Marion County history page was read and has no fire tower mention.
